level: stop-fence slice 4, reentrant declared-client revocation adapter with real Agent persistence, offline and partial recovery; component evidence only
componentAcceptance: Win11: quarantineMigrationRemoteClients prevalidates every declared config/machine/client identity, invokes the real Agent admin CLI and accepts completion only after reading back revoked=1 from the real Agent SQLite with an unchanged config SHA-256. Real tests cover successful revoke and idempotent reentry, offline retry, a two-Agent partial failure that resumes only the second unconfirmed client, and identity mismatch with zero revoke calls. The suite passes four consecutive tests in each of three runs; the E97/E98 combination passes 5/5 and the full root regression has zero failures.
productAcceptance: None. The component is not yet called by migration drain. It covers only declared clients and does not drain in-flight effects, cover other clients or machines, stop direct OS writers, enable activation or provide rollback/release. Scores remain 0/20, 1/63 and M0 11/12; stopWriteProvable, activationSupported and postActivationRollbackSupported remain false.
implementation: The owner-only adapter accepts bounded configPath/machineId/clientId declarations. Canonical non-symlink paths, all target identities and the real client rows are checked before the first mutation.

Each real CLI revoke is followed by a fresh SQLite read of machine identity, client revoked state and config digest. Unconfirmed failure reports the current target, completed targets and the original cause.
Durable revoked state is the recovery journal: already-revoked rows skip CLI execution, so an offline first attempt can be retried and a two-Agent partial failure resumes only the unfinished target.
An optional trusted runtime launches a trusted JavaScript CLI with an argv array and no shell. This is required on Windows, where direct spawn of .mjs fails with EFTYPE.

The result declares only credential admission blocking and persistent exclusion for its explicit clients. External restart, persistent external exclusion and stopWriteProvable stay false. The native suite is registered in npm test.
testRuns: New suite: three consecutive standalone runs, each 4 tests / 4 pass / 0 fail.
E97 real authorization fence + E98 recovery adapter: 5 tests / 5 pass / 0 fail.
Final npm test: phase one 1587/1583/0/4 and phase two 354/274/0/80; total 1941 tests, 1857 pass, 0 fail, 84 skipped.
preservedFailures: The first suite run failed three of four tests: direct Windows spawn of the .mjs CLI returned EFTYPE, so the first real revoke and subsequent partial-failure expectations were unconfirmed. The original cause is now preserved on the error.
The fix adds an explicit trusted Node runtime rather than skipping post-revoke verification. The corrected real suite passes all four cases repeatedly.
limitations: The adapter is not yet called by migration drain or the hash-chain orchestrator; this is a callable component, not product activation wiring.
It does not prove draining of effects already executing when revocation starts. Other clients, machines, unknown writers and direct OS access remain outside the declaration.
Remote deployment invocation, rotate/reauthorization, release and machine reboot remain open.
No real user profile, model inference, production process, push or release was used.
